recipes.name: Eggplant Balls
ingredients_raw: 0.75 cup dry bread crumbs, or more as needed

steps.text: Heat oil in a medium skillet over medium heat. Add garlic and sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Stir in eggplant and water. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and steam until eggplant is soft, about 20 minutes.
Transfer to a large bowl and let cool for 5 to 10 minutes.

Add parsley, bread crumbs, Parmesan, and eggs to eggplant; mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until thoroughly combined and mixture can be rolled into balls. Add more bread crumbs as needed to make mixture workable. Cover and refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a baking sheet.
Roll chilled eggplant mixture into 18 balls; place onto the prepared baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes. Serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Eggplant Balls
raw_recipe.description: These eggplant 'meatballs' made with tender eggplant, bread crumbs, and Parmesan are baked for a juicy meat-free option to serve with pasta and marinara sauce.

review.reviewBody: Very good, but here's what I did differently the second time I made this dish. I skinned the Eggplant, cubed it, and marinated it in Soy Sauce for 20 minutes. I used more than 8 cloves of Garlic ( 12 ). I used a store bought variety of seasoned Bread Crumbs ( Italian ) and found that mashing the cooked Eggplant aided in the mixing of the ingredients. Excellent!!!

Aunt Mary's Eggplant Balls by Lynette Marie. Peeled eggplant, 1/2t each onion powder & garlic powder; 1t dried parsley. 'Ended up adding 2c & it still could've used more really; or one less egg(?) Try cornbread crumbs with cornbread dressing seasonings or more crumbs with traditional bread dressing seasonings & having hits. Put on a toothpick for a holiday appetizer. Note4Me: sugg: add 2T Balsamic, spices/Italian bread crumbs. One less eggs has ya not adding more breadcrumbs. Add 1t red pepper & 2 or mo

Fantastic! Just altered it a little for preference....salted the chopped, peeled eggplant and let rest for 30 min in a colander in the sink. Sautéed the garlic with a bit of red pepper flakes before adding the eggplant, then I used broth for the water for steaming. After it cooled, I only had Panko...then added Italian Seasoning to make up for the 'blah' factor...added the other items per recipe. The mixture sat in the fridge 30 min and then I balled them up, sprayed them with olive oil and air fried them on 350 till they were brown, turning half way. I served them over zuchinni noodles topped with a spicy tomatillo marinara sauce. The meat-eating man was crazy about them!

It was good but I think it could be great with some changes. It was a little too wet, so I think I would salt the eggplant to get rid of some of the water, then roast it uncovered to get rid of even more. I would use cooked bulgur instead of breadcrumbs to give it a little more chew. Then I would form it into patties instead of balls and fry them in a little oil to get a good crust on both sides.

My husband and daughter love eggplant, my son and I not so much. This has been a great option for our family of four. I'm a vegetarian so I've made them into patties, varying the seasoning, and eaten it on nights the family is eating meat. They make great meatball sandwiches and of course spaghetti and meatballs. I make a double batch of this every week while harvesting my eggplant and freeze them. I use Japanese eggplant. If you chop it up in the food processor the final product has the look and consistency of meat. Even my eggplant hating sister will eat patties made this way, with lots of condiments, of course.

Loved these eggplant balls! They only thing I changed was cooking of the eggplant. I cut a large eggplant in half, brushed the cut sides with olive oil, salt and pepper. Roasted it, cut side down along with a whole head of garlic on a sprayed cookie sheet @400 degrees for 30 minutes until soft. Cool until easy to handle. Scraped the eggplant into a bowl, squeezed half the roasted garlic on top then added the rest of the ingredients.

I love the idea of this recipe, I just didn't think it would have enough flavor written as is. I used 3/4 of a cup of Italian seasoned bread crumbs, 1/2 of a cup of parmesan cheese, 1 teaspoon each of basil, oregano and parsley, 1 egg and no water (I didn't sweat the eggplant), oh and I peeled the eggplant (personal preference). It's a great recipe, I just like a punch more flavor

Very good recipe! I had an eggplant I wanted to use up, so I tried this recipe. In the end, I didn’t have enough eggplant, so I added mushrooms. Worked great and is still delicious. I wanted to pass that on to anyone who may end up in that position. I’m also going to line the baking pan with parchment paper next time. The bottoms of the eggplant balls had a harder edge that detracts from enjoying them. I’m going to try less baking time, too. I think these would be great on an Italian roll, or maybe garlic bread, with a little sauce and cheese. Maybe on a pizza…? I really enjoyed them! Since I have mostly a plant-based diet, I know I’ll be making them again soon.

These are beyond delicious. I made these both ways, with skin and without. Without the skin and peeled makes a more moist, consistent meatball. And aside from the fresh parsley, I added in the same amount of fresh chopped Basil. After baking, added them to my sauce for even better flavor! Don't need to eat the Meat ones ever gain! Thanks Mary!

My hubby LOVES eggplant and I would turn my nose up to it..didn't like the texture..but eggplant made this way is AWESOME!! I only used 1 beaten egg and seasoned up with 2 teaspoons onion powder and 2 teaspoons of Italian seasoning. I also substituted dried parsley for fresh, using 1/8 cup...These are addicting!! Freeze wonderfully..Now if I am hungry I pop a few in the microwave for a minute, top with sauce and eat on a bun!!

This is a lovely recipe! One of the best eggplant balls that I have ever tasted! I had a large eggplant that gave me 8 cups so I decided to try this recipe first as written, and then again with minor modifications. I did find the baked version to be a bit bland but went really well with aioli. The second time around I slightly browned the garlic, which added more of a garlicky taste, and I also added a bit of salt. I fried the balls in a bit of EVOO (about 1/4 inch of oil in frying pan) and it really boosted the flavour. To prevent it from falling apart, cut the eggplant into tiny cubes (1/4-1/2 an inch). This will help hold it's shape when cooked. I was also surprised how well the parsley works well with the eggplant (I would have used basil instead). This is my go-to recipe for eggplant balls. Thank you for sharing this recipe, Lynette Marie!!
I roasted the eggplant as others suggested and followed the rest of the recipe. My whole family l8ked it!

I added chopped basil too. The secret is to let the bread crumbs soak a bit into the mix and then roll into balls. I fried mine. Will try baking next time too. The smell in the kitchen all day was wonderful!
I made sure I squeezed a lot of the moisture out of the cubed eggplant before I sauté them. I also added some grated goat milk mozzarella.

I peeled the eggplant and marinated in soy sauce. I also used 10 cloves of garlic, and a dash of onion powder, Italian seasoning, and oregano, and and added extra panko breadcrumbs. I didn't have eggs on hand so I used aquafaba. I used a small cookie scoop so that the size was uniform. Next time I'll add more breadcrumbs
Love this recipe wouldn't change a thing.

pretty good. i added seasonings as the eggplant cooked (salt, black pepper, chili flakes, smoked paprika + some soy sauce and mirin) and added some caramelised onions and a lot more grated garlic into the mixture. I also just put it on the air fryer instead of the oven, for 15 minutes, and it got really nice.
Very good!!! I added Tajin and a little extra salt. They crisped up nicely!!
Big hit eggplant is a big pleaser in the family. Great new way to have it .

I followed the directions except I forgot to chill for 15 min. The eggplant was fork soft, but there was no way to make balls or patties so it became a casserole. A little too eggy tasting for me but otherwise good. The fresh parsley was nice.
